key_insight: RayPE replaces standard token positions on the 2D/temporal grid with a ray-space encoding that reflects actual 3D camera geometry. It uses the Plücker reciprocal product to model relations between rays, giving video diffusion transformers a more scene-aware positional signal.
problem_solved: Existing video diffusion transformers use RoPE on (u,v,t), which encodes where a token is sampled in the camera grid but not how different views relate in 3D space. This makes it harder for models to learn consistent geometry across viewpoints and time.
method: Represent camera rays in ray space rather than only using image-plane and time coordinates.
Compute pairwise ray relations with the Plücker reciprocal product, which is bilinear and aligns naturally with attention computation.
Inject this ray-space positional encoding into video diffusion transformers to improve 3D-aware generation.
impact: For practitioners, RayPE offers a drop-in way to make video generation models better at respecting 3D structure and multi-view consistency. This can improve realism, viewpoint coherence, and geometric stability in generated videos.

paper_title: RayPE: Ray-Space Positional Encoding for 3D-Aware Video Generation
paper_authors: Minghao Yin, Jiahao Lu, Wenbo Hu, Wang Zhao, Shan Ying
